title: Property disputes between siblings - mediation vs litigation
p1: Two siblings inherit a property. Within months, a family relationship turns into a courtroom battle. But what if the biggest mistake is choosing a fight before exploring another path?
p2: Many people assume litigation is the only way to settle ownership disputes. A surprising fact: a court case may decide who gets what, but it often cannot repair the damage done to family relationships. Mediation gives siblings a chance to discuss solutions with a neutral person helping them reach an agreement.
p3: Mediation can be useful when siblings want flexibility — such as selling the property, one sibling buying out another, or creating a fair usage plan. Litigation may still be necessary when there is no cooperation or serious legal disagreement. The key is choosing a process that matches the situation, not reacting out of anger. Before filing a case, consider whether a structured conversation could save time, money, and relationships.
conclusion: If you were involved in a sibling property dispute, would you try mediation first or go directly to court?
